title: Two out of three for perfect complexes
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let K, L, and M be objects of the derived category D(\mathcal{O}_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. If K\to L\to M\to K[1] is a distinguished triangle and two of K, L, and M are perfect complexes [def-pc-perfect-complex], then the third is perfect.

proof.text: Given perfect first and second terms, [lem-pc-perfect-common-affine-models] supplies at each point one affine open and strictly perfect models for both terms. Apply [lem-pc-perfect-affine-cone-model] on that open. The resulting local models of the third term satisfy the definition [def-pc-perfect-complex], proving the first two-out-of-three implication.

Perfectness is invariant under isomorphism: map the inverse isomorphism through each open restriction and compose it with the representing isomorphism. It is invariant under any integer shift: replace a local model $K$ with $K[n]$, replace its bounds $a,b$ with $a-n,b-n$, and use the same finite-free retract pair in degree $i+n$. The commutation isomorphisms of exact restriction and $Q$ with shifts give the required derived isomorphism.

If the last two terms are perfect, rotate by TR2 [def-weil-triangulated-category] and apply the first case to obtain perfection of $T_1[1]$. Shift by $-1$ and transport across the canonical cancellation isomorphism to prove perfection of $T_1$. If the first and last terms are perfect, inverse-rotate to $T_3[-1]\to T_1\to T_2$; shift invariance and the first case prove perfection of $T_2$.
